questions.q: Can't we just tell it to write clean code?
questions.a: It helps the start, not the trend. In SlopCodeBench, explicit quality guidance cut the starting verbosity and erosion “by up to a third, without affecting degradation rates.” The code began cleaner and got worse just as fast, so measure the slope, not one snapshot.

teach.title: How it works: measuring a run of tasks

questions.q: Isn't this just the context window filling up over 20 tasks?
questions.a: Not mainly. SlopCodeBench gives the agent no record of its earlier conversation at each step, only the code (“we do not provide the prior conversation's context”), and quality still fell in most runs. The damage lives in the repo, so a bigger memory won't remove it.

questions.q: If the tests pass, why would the team care?
questions.a: Because reviewers pay for what tests don't check. In METR's August 2025 study, Claude 3.7 Sonnet had an average success rate of 38% on 18 open-source issues, by the maintainers' tests, but none of the 15 changes reviewed by hand could be merged as-is. Even the ones that passed needed about 26 minutes of human fixing each: missing tests, documentation, lint and style problems.

teach.title: How it works: measuring a run of tasks

questions.q: What does “stateless” mean for a coding benchmark?
questions.a: Every task starts from the same clean, human-written version of the repo, which is reset after each task. The agent never has to build on its own earlier changes.

teach.title: How it works: measuring a run of tasks

questions.q: Name three things to track across a long chain of tasks in one repo.
questions.a: Success at each step with no reset; whether earlier tasks' tests still pass; and the repo's health, such as complexity and copied code. Then compare with the same tasks scored one at a time.

questions.q: What did the SWE-STEPS study find when it ran the tasks as a chain, with no reset between them?
questions.a: Scores fell. On its Mini set, Claude Sonnet 4.5 went from 66.25% of pull requests solved with a reset after each one to 43.75% without. On its Lite set, Gemini 3 Flash went from 56.52% to 36.59%.
